title: Tafseer Foundations
subtitle: Understanding the meanings of Al-Isti'adhah, Al-Basmalah, Al-Fatihah, and the short Surahs of Juz Amma (Al-Asr to An-Nas)
description: A three-level journey through the Tafseer of the short Surahs of Juz Amma — from the opening of the Qur'an (Al-Isti'adhah, Al-Basmalah, Al-Fatihah) through the stories and lessons of the final Surahs, to a deeper reflection on Tawhid, protection, and faith.

difficulties.label: Beginner
difficulties.description: Opening the Qur'an — Isti'adhah, Basmalah, Al-Fatihah, Al-'Asr & Al-Humazah

stages.title: Al-Isti'adhah (I) — Meaning & Purpose
stages.description: What seeking refuge before recitation means and why it matters

questions.text: What is the meaning of الاستعاذة؟
options: Seeking protection from Allah
Beginning a Surah
Praising Allah
Making du'a only
questions.answer: Seeking protection from Allah

questions.text: From what do we specifically seek refuge when starting to recite the Qur'an?
options: From Shaytan, the accursed devil
From other people
From hunger
From forgetfulness only
questions.answer: From Shaytan, the accursed devil

questions.text: معنى الاستعاذة هو:
options: نطلب الحماية من الله
نشكر الله
نستغفر الله
نحمد الناس
questions.answer: نطلب الحماية من الله

questions.text: Why is Isti'adhah legislated before reciting the Qur'an?
options: To protect the heart from Shaytan's whispers that could distract from reflecting on the Qur'an
To end the recitation properly
To praise the reciter's voice
To ask Allah for provision
questions.answer: To protect the heart from Shaytan's whispers that could distract from reflecting on the Qur'an

questions.text: Is Al-Isti'adhah considered part of the actual text of the Qur'an?
options: No, it is a supplication recited before starting recitation, not part of the Mushaf text
Yes, it is the first verse of every surah
Yes, but only in Al-Fatihah
No, it is only recited after finishing
questions.answer: No, it is a supplication recited before starting recitation, not part of the Mushaf text

stages.title: Al-Isti'adhah (II) — The Wording
stages.description: Understanding أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ word by word

questions.text: What does "أَعُوذُ" mean?
options: I seek refuge / I seek protection
I praise
I thank
I remember
questions.answer: I seek refuge / I seek protection

questions.text: "بِاللَّهِ" tells us with whom we take refuge. Who is that?
options: Allah alone
The angels
The Prophet ﷺ
One's parents
questions.answer: Allah alone

questions.text: What does "الشيطان" refer to?
options: Shaytan / the devil (Iblis and his party)
A type of jinn that helps people
A disobedient human
An angel of punishment
questions.answer: Shaytan / the devil (Iblis and his party)

questions.text: معنى كلمة "الرجيم" هو:
options: القوي
الغني
المطرود من رحمة الله
العادل
questions.answer: المطرود من رحمة الله

questions.text: Put together, "أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ" means:
options: I seek refuge in Allah from Shaytan, the accursed/expelled one
I praise Allah, the Most Merciful
I ask Allah for guidance on the straight path
I thank Allah for His blessings
questions.answer: I seek refuge in Allah from Shaytan, the accursed/expelled one

stages.title: Al-Isti'adhah (III) — Rulings & Lessons
stages.description: When Isti'adhah is legislated, and the lessons it teaches the heart

questions.text: What is the ruling on saying Isti'adhah before reciting the Qur'an, according to the majority of scholars?
options: Recommended (Mustahabb), not obligatory
Obligatory (Wajib) in every case
Forbidden outside of prayer
Only for reciters, never for listeners
questions.answer: Recommended (Mustahabb), not obligatory

questions.text: Which verse commands seeking refuge before recitation?
options: Surah An-Nahl 16:98
Surah Al-Fatihah 1:1
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:1
Surah An-Nas 114:1
questions.answer: Surah An-Nahl 16:98

questions.text: الاستعاذة تُقال أيضا في أوقات أخرى مثل:
options: الغضب والخوف والوسوسة
الأكل فقط
النوم فقط
الخروج من المنزل فقط
questions.answer: الغضب والخوف والوسوسة

questions.text: What is a key lesson from beginning recitation with Isti'adhah?
options: We acknowledge our weakness and need for Allah's protection before engaging in worship
We show off our knowledge of Arabic
We remind Shaytan of his fate
We complete an obligatory pillar of prayer
questions.answer: We acknowledge our weakness and need for Allah's protection before engaging in worship

questions.text: True or False: Isti'adhah shows that Shaytan actively tries to prevent people from benefiting from the Qur'an.
options: True
False
questions.answer: True

stages.title: Al-Basmalah (I) — Meaning & Occurrence
stages.description: What Bismillah means and where it appears in the Qur'an

questions.text: What does "بِسْمِ اللَّهِ" mean?
options: In the name of Allah
Praise be to Allah
I seek refuge in Allah
Glory be to Allah
questions.answer: In the name of Allah

questions.text: The Basmalah appears at the start of every surah except one. Which surah does not begin with it?
options: At-Tawbah (Surah 9)
Al-Baqarah (Surah 2)
Al-Ikhlas (Surah 112)
An-Nas (Surah 114)
questions.answer: At-Tawbah (Surah 9)

questions.text: معنى البسملة هو:
options: نبدأ عملنا باسم الله طلبا للبركة والإعانة
نطلب المغفرة من الله
نحمد الله على نعمه
نستعيذ بالله من الشيطان
questions.answer: نبدأ عملنا باسم الله طلبا للبركة والإعانة

questions.text: Why do Muslims say Bismillah before actions like eating?
options: To seek Allah's blessing and help, and to remember Him at the start of any deed
Because it is a pillar of Islam
To replace the obligatory prayer
Because it is only a cultural custom
questions.answer: To seek Allah's blessing and help, and to remember Him at the start of any deed

questions.text: The Basmalah is also found inside a surah's body (not just its opening) in one place. Which surah?
options: An-Naml (Surah 27)
Al-Kahf (Surah 18)
Maryam (Surah 19)
Yusuf (Surah 12)
questions.answer: An-Naml (Surah 27)

stages.title: Al-Basmalah (II) — Allah, Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim
stages.description: Understanding the three names of Allah gathered in one verse

questions.text: "اللَّهُ" is:
options: The proper name of the One true God, unique to Him alone
A general word meaning 'a god'
A title given only to angels
A name used for idols
questions.answer: The proper name of the One true God, unique to Him alone

questions.text: "الرَّحْمَٰنُ" refers to:
options: Allah's all-encompassing mercy that covers all of creation
Allah's mercy reserved only for the believers
Allah's power to punish
Allah's knowledge of the unseen
questions.answer: Allah's all-encompassing mercy that covers all of creation

questions.text: "الرَّحِيمُ" refers to:
options: Allah's special mercy reserved for the believers, especially in the Hereafter
Allah's mercy toward animals only
A mercy limited to this world only
A name exclusive to the angels
questions.answer: Allah's special mercy reserved for the believers, especially in the Hereafter

questions.text: ما الفرق بين الرحمن والرحيم؟
options: الرحمن رحمته لكل الخلق، والرحيم رحمته خاصة بالمؤمنين
لا فرق بينهما إطلاقا
الرحمن للدنيا والرحيم للحيوانات
الرحيم أعظم من الرحمن في كل شيء
questions.answer: الرحمن رحمته لكل الخلق، والرحيم رحمته خاصة بالمؤمنين

questions.text: Both Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim come from which root?
options: رحم (mercy)
حمد (praise)
عبد (worship)
ملك (ownership)
questions.answer: رحم (mercy)

stages.title: Al-Basmalah (III) — Rulings & Lessons
stages.description: The virtue of starting affairs with Allah's name, and its scholarly status in Al-Fatihah

questions.text: What is the ruling on saying Bismillah before eating?
options: Recommended and emphasized
Obligatory like the five daily prayers
Forbidden while eating with others
Only required on Fridays
questions.answer: Recommended and emphasized

questions.text: According to hadith, what may happen if a person eats without saying Bismillah?
options: Shaytan may share in that food with him
The food loses all nutritional value
He must repeat his ablution
Nothing changes at all
questions.answer: Shaytan may share in that food with him

questions.text: البسملة تدل على:
options: الاستعانة بالله والتبرك باسمه
الاستغناء عن الدعاء
إنهاء العمل بنجاح
التوبة من الذنوب
questions.answer: الاستعانة بالله والتبرك باسمه

questions.text: The Basmalah combines two of Allah's names of mercy back-to-back. What does this teach us?
options: Allah's mercy should be our first hope when beginning any matter
Mercy is less important than justice
Only prophets deserve Allah's mercy
Mercy applies only after death
questions.answer: Allah's mercy should be our first hope when beginning any matter

questions.text: Is the Basmalah counted as the first verse of Al-Fatihah by all scholars?
options: No — scholars differ, though all agree it is legislated to be recited
Yes, unanimously, without any difference of opinion
No, and no scholar considers it part of the Qur'an at all
Yes, but only in the Hanafi school
questions.answer: No — scholars differ, though all agree it is legislated to be recited

stages.title: Al-Fatihah (I) — Names & Virtues
stages.description: Why Al-Fatihah is called Umm al-Kitab and why every prayer needs it

questions.text: Why is Al-Fatihah called "Umm al-Kitab" (Mother of the Book)?
options: Because it contains the essential themes of the entire Qur'an in summary
Because it was the first surah revealed chronologically
Because it is the longest surah
Because it has no virtue over other surahs
questions.answer: Because it contains the essential themes of the entire Qur'an in summary

questions.text: Al-Fatihah is also called "As-Sab' al-Mathani", meaning:
options: The seven oft-repeated verses
The seven heavens
The seven names of Allah
The seven pillars of faith
questions.answer: The seven oft-repeated verses

questions.text: How many times, at minimum, does a Muslim recite Al-Fatihah each day through the five prayers?
options: At least 17 times
Exactly 5 times
At least 33 times
Only once a day
questions.answer: At least 17 times

questions.text: True or False: No prayer is valid without reciting Al-Fatihah, according to authentic hadith.
options: True
False
questions.answer: True

questions.text: كم عدد آيات سورة الفاتحة؟
options: سبع آيات
خمس آيات
عشر آيات
ثلاث آيات
questions.answer: سبع آيات

stages.title: Al-Fatihah (II) — Praise & Lordship
stages.description: Unpacking Al-Hamdu Lillahi Rabbil 'Alameen

questions.text: "الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ" means:
options: All praise belongs to Allah alone
Glory be to Allah
I seek refuge in Allah
Allah is the Greatest
questions.answer: All praise belongs to Allah alone

questions.text: Why does Al-Hamd (praise) belong to Allah exclusively?
options: Because He alone is perfect in His attributes and deserving of praise for all He has created and bestowed
Because no one else exists in creation
Because praise is only a linguistic formality
Because angels demand it
questions.answer: Because He alone is perfect in His attributes and deserving of praise for all He has created and bestowed

questions.text: "رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ" means:
options: Lord of all the worlds (all of creation)
King of the Arabs only
Lord of the angels only
Owner of the Ka'bah only
questions.answer: Lord of all the worlds (all of creation)

questions.text: معنى "العالمين":
options: كل ما سوى الله من المخلوقات
الملائكة فقط
الإنس فقط
السماوات فقط
questions.answer: كل ما سوى الله من المخلوقات

questions.text: What does calling Allah "Rabb" (Lord) here primarily establish?
options: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah — that Allah alone creates, owns, and sustains everything
That Allah shares His lordship with the angels
That Allah only sustains the believers
That 'Rabb' is a title reserved for kings
questions.answer: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah — that Allah alone creates, owns, and sustains everything

stages.title: Al-Fatihah (III) — Mercy & the Day of Judgment
stages.description: Understanding Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim, Maliki Yawmid-Din

questions.text: Why are "Ar-Rahman" and "Ar-Rahim" repeated here, after already appearing in the Basmalah?
options: To emphasize Allah's vast mercy right after mentioning His Lordship, balancing awe with hope
Because of a copying mistake preserved in recitation
To fill out the verse count to seven
Because the Basmalah is not really part of the surah at all
questions.answer: To emphasize Allah's vast mercy right after mentioning His Lordship, balancing awe with hope

questions.text: "مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ" means:
options: Master/Owner of the Day of Judgment
King of this worldly life
Owner of the Ka'bah
Lord of the angels
questions.answer: Master/Owner of the Day of Judgment

questions.text: "يَوْمِ الدِّينِ" refers to:
options: The Day of Recompense/Judgment
The day of the Hijrah
The day Adam was created
Friday, specifically
questions.answer: The Day of Recompense/Judgment

questions.text: Some qira'at (readings) render this word as "مَلِكِ" instead of "مَالِكِ". What is the difference?
options: Malik means 'King,' while Maalik means 'Owner/Master' — both readings are authentic and their meanings complement each other
Malik is incorrect and was never a valid reading
They are spelled the same with no difference at all
Maalik refers to angels while Malik refers to Allah
questions.answer: Malik means 'King,' while Maalik means 'Owner/Master' — both readings are authentic and their meanings complement each other

questions.text: Why mention the Day of Judgment right after Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim?
options: To balance hope in Allah's mercy with awareness of accountability
To scare the reciter away from worship
Because mercy and judgment are unrelated topics
To end the surah's praise section abruptly
questions.answer: To balance hope in Allah's mercy with awareness of accountability

stages.title: Al-Fatihah (IV) — Worship & Seeking Help
stages.description: Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in — the turning point of the surah

questions.text: "إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ" means:
options: You alone we worship
You alone we praise
You alone we fear
You alone we obey blindly
questions.answer: You alone we worship

questions.text: "وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ" means:
options: And You alone we ask for help
And You alone we thank
And You alone we remember
And You alone we follow
questions.answer: And You alone we ask for help

questions.text: Why does "نَعْبُدُ" (worship) come before "نَسْتَعِينُ" (seeking help)?
options: Because worship is the goal and seeking help is the means to accomplish it, so the goal is mentioned first
Because seeking help is more important than worship
There is no reason; the order is arbitrary
Because Arabic grammar requires verbs before objects
questions.answer: Because worship is the goal and seeking help is the means to accomplish it, so the goal is mentioned first

questions.text: This ayah marks a shift in the surah's address, from speaking about Allah to speaking directly to Him. What is this called?
options: Iltifat (a shift in address)
Isti'adhah
Tafsir bil-Ma'thur
Naskh
questions.answer: Iltifat (a shift in address)

questions.text: What does this ayah teach about worship and reliance on Allah (tawakkul)?
options: True worship cannot be achieved without seeking Allah's help, and we should rely on no one else for it
Worship and seeking help are two unrelated acts
Only prophets need to seek Allah's help
Seeking help from Allah replaces the need to worship Him
questions.answer: True worship cannot be achieved without seeking Allah's help, and we should rely on no one else for it

stages.title: Al-Fatihah (V) — The Straight Path
stages.description: Ihdinas-Siratal Mustaqim and the three groups of people mentioned

questions.text: "اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ" means:
options: Guide us to the straight path
Protect us from the Fire
Forgive us our sins
Grant us provision
questions.answer: Guide us to the straight path

questions.text: "صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ" refers to:
options: The path of those Allah has favored (the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, the righteous)
The path of the wealthy
The path of the earlier nations only
The path of the angels alone
questions.answer: The path of those Allah has favored (the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, the righteous)

questions.text: "غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ" is most commonly explained by commentators as referring to:
options: Those who knew the truth but rejected it deliberately
Those who never received any revelation
The angels who disobeyed Allah
The idol-worshippers of Makkah specifically
questions.answer: Those who knew the truth but rejected it deliberately

questions.text: "وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ" is most commonly explained by commentators as referring to:
options: Those who worship or act without knowledge, going astray
Those who follow the straight path perfectly
The prophets and messengers
Those who never sinned
questions.answer: Those who worship or act without knowledge, going astray

questions.text: Why do we ask for guidance to the Straight Path even though we are already believers?
options: Because we need Allah's constant guidance to remain firm and increase in it every moment of our lives
Because the request is only symbolic and has no real meaning
Because believers are exempt from ever going astray
Because this du'a is only for new Muslims
questions.answer: Because we need Allah's constant guidance to remain firm and increase in it every moment of our lives

stages.title: Al-Fatihah (VI) — Structure & Lessons
stages.description: How Al-Fatihah is divided, and its overall message

questions.text: A hadith qudsi describes Al-Fatihah as divided between Allah and His servant. What is this division?
options: The first half (praise of Allah) is for Allah, and the second half (asking for guidance) is for the servant
The first half is for men and the second for women
It is divided equally between the five daily prayers
It has no such division; this is a misconception
questions.answer: The first half (praise of Allah) is for Allah, and the second half (asking for guidance) is for the servant

questions.text: What are the three main sections of Al-Fatihah?
options: Praise of Allah, then a declaration of worship & reliance, then a supplication for guidance
History, law, and prophecy
Creation, judgment, and paradise
Warning, promise, and story
questions.answer: Praise of Allah, then a declaration of worship & reliance, then a supplication for guidance

questions.text: Why is Al-Fatihah recited in every rak'ah rather than just once in the prayer?
options: Because it summarizes the purpose of the entire prayer and life itself
Because it is the shortest surah in the Qur'an
Because the other surahs cannot be repeated
Because it was revealed multiple times
questions.answer: Because it summarizes the purpose of the entire prayer and life itself

questions.text: What balance does Al-Fatihah teach every believer to maintain?
options: A balance between hope in Allah's mercy and fear of the Day of Judgment
A balance between wealth and poverty
A balance between speech and silence
A balance between fasting and eating
questions.answer: A balance between hope in Allah's mercy and fear of the Day of Judgment

questions.text: In one sentence, what is the overall theme of Surah Al-Fatihah?
options: It is a complete supplication teaching the servant how to praise Allah and ask Him for the straight path
It is mainly a historical narrative about past nations
It is a set of legal rulings on inheritance
It is a description of Paradise and Hellfire
questions.answer: It is a complete supplication teaching the servant how to praise Allah and ask Him for the straight path

stages.title: Al-'Asr (I) — The Oath by Time
stages.description: Why Allah swears by time, and the default state of mankind

questions.text: "وَالْعَصْرِ" — Allah swears by what?
options: Time / the passing of time
The sun
The night
The Ka'bah
questions.answer: Time / the passing of time

questions.text: Why does Allah swear by time in this surah?
options: To draw attention to its value and how central it is to human loss or gain
Because time is worshipped in Islam
Because it has no real significance
To indicate the surah is very long
questions.answer: To draw attention to its value and how central it is to human loss or gain

questions.text: "إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ" means:
options: Indeed, mankind is in loss
Indeed, mankind is successful
Indeed, mankind is asleep
Indeed, mankind is patient
questions.answer: Indeed, mankind is in loss

questions.text: What is the general default state of every human being according to this surah, unless an exception applies?
options: A state of loss (khusr)
A state of guaranteed success
A state of wealth
A state of knowledge
questions.answer: A state of loss (khusr)

questions.text: Imam Ash-Shafi'i famously said about this surah that:
options: If people only reflected on it, it would be sufficient for them
It was the first surah ever revealed
It should be recited only in Ramadan
It replaces the need for Al-Fatihah in prayer
questions.answer: If people only reflected on it, it would be sufficient for them

stages.title: Al-'Asr (II) — The Four Conditions
stages.description: The four things that save a person from loss

questions.text: What is the first condition for salvation mentioned in Surah Al-'Asr?
options: Iman (faith/belief)
Wealth
Knowledge of Arabic
Physical strength
questions.answer: Iman (faith/belief)

questions.text: The second condition, "وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ", means:
options: And did righteous deeds
And spoke the truth
And remained silent
And traveled far
questions.answer: And did righteous deeds

questions.text: "وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ" means:
options: And advised/enjoined one another to the truth
And competed with one another in wealth
And argued with one another
And avoided one another
questions.answer: And advised/enjoined one another to the truth

questions.text: The fourth condition, "وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ", means:
options: And advised/enjoined one another to patience
And advised one another to haste
And advised one another to silence
And advised one another to wealth
questions.answer: And advised/enjoined one another to patience

questions.text: ما هي الشروط الأربعة للنجاة من الخسران في سورة العصر؟
options: الإيمان، والعمل الصالح، والتواصي بالحق، والتواصي بالصبر
الصلاة والصيام والحج والزكاة
العلم والمال والصحة والوقت
الصبر والشكر والتوبة والدعاء
questions.answer: الإيمان، والعمل الصالح، والتواصي بالحق، والتواصي بالصبر

stages.title: Al-'Asr (III) — Lessons
stages.description: Why all four conditions must come together, and what this teaches about time

questions.text: Why must belief (Iman) come before righteous deeds in the surah's order?
options: Because correct belief is the foundation upon which acceptable deeds are built
Because deeds have no relation to belief at all
Because righteous deeds are impossible for believers
Because the order has no meaning
questions.answer: Because correct belief is the foundation upon which acceptable deeds are built

questions.text: Why does advising others to truth and patience matter for salvation, not just personal deeds?
options: Because a complete believer helps others as well as reforming themselves
Because it is easier than doing good deeds oneself
Because it replaces the need for personal righteousness
Because it is only recommended, never important
questions.answer: Because a complete believer helps others as well as reforming themselves

questions.text: What does "patience" (Sabr) refer to in this surah's context?
options: Patience in obeying Allah, avoiding sin, and enduring hardship while calling to the truth
Patience only in financial matters
Patience only during fasting
Patience only with family members
questions.answer: Patience in obeying Allah, avoiding sin, and enduring hardship while calling to the truth

questions.text: What overall lesson does Surah Al-'Asr teach about time?
options: Time is a precious asset that, if not used in faith and good deeds, results in loss
Time has no real value in Islam
Time should only be spent working for wealth
Time is only relevant to the wealthy
questions.answer: Time is a precious asset that, if not used in faith and good deeds, results in loss

questions.text: True or False: Simply having faith without good deeds is enough to be saved from loss according to this surah.
options: False
True
questions.answer: False

stages.title: Al-Humazah (I) — The Mocker & Backbiter
stages.description: The meaning of Humazah and Lumazah, and the occasion of revelation

questions.text: "وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ" — what does "الهمزة" mean?
options: One who mocks/slanders people, whether to their face or behind their backs
One who is extremely generous
One who prays a lot
One who travels frequently
questions.answer: One who mocks/slanders people, whether to their face or behind their backs

questions.text: "اللمزة" specifically emphasizes:
options: Slandering/defaming people, often behind their backs, through words
Giving charity secretly
Reciting the Qur'an beautifully
Helping the poor
questions.answer: Slandering/defaming people, often behind their backs, through words

questions.text: "وَيْلٌ" at the start of the surah expresses:
options: A severe warning/threat
A simple greeting
A statement of joy
A question
questions.answer: A severe warning/threat

questions.text: According to tafsir, this surah was revealed concerning people who:
options: Mocked and slandered others, especially the poor, while boasting about their own wealth
Fought in the Battle of Badr
Migrated to Madinah
Built the Ka'bah
questions.answer: Mocked and slandered others, especially the poor, while boasting about their own wealth

questions.text: Why does the surah combine "backbiting" and "love of wealth" as connected sins?
options: Because arrogance from wealth often leads a person to look down on and mock others
Because they are entirely unrelated topics placed together randomly
Because wealthy people never sin in other ways
Because backbiting always leads to wealth
questions.answer: Because arrogance from wealth often leads a person to look down on and mock others

stages.title: Al-Humazah (II) — Love of Wealth
stages.description: The mistaken belief that wealth grants permanence

questions.text: "الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ" describes someone who:
options: Collected wealth and kept counting/hoarding it
Gave away his wealth in charity
Lost all his wealth
Refused to work for wealth
questions.answer: Collected wealth and kept counting/hoarding it

questions.text: "يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ" means this person thinks:
options: His wealth will make him live forever (immortal)
His wealth will be inherited justly
His wealth will be taken away soon
His wealth belongs to Allah
questions.answer: His wealth will make him live forever (immortal)

questions.text: What is the core mistaken belief being condemned in this ayah?
options: That wealth can grant permanence or protect one from death and accountability
That wealth should always be shared with the poor
That wealth is inherently evil
That wealth cannot be earned honestly
questions.answer: That wealth can grant permanence or protect one from death and accountability

questions.text: What attitude toward wealth does this surah warn against?
options: Obsessively hoarding and counting wealth while forgetting Allah and the Hereafter
Spending wealth on one's family
Saving wealth for emergencies
Earning wealth through honest work
questions.answer: Obsessively hoarding and counting wealth while forgetting Allah and the Hereafter

questions.text: يحسب أن ماله أخلده - ما الخطأ في هذا الاعتقاد؟
options: لا شيء يخلد الإنسان في الدنيا، والمال لا ينفعه يوم القيامة
المال يخلد صاحبه فعلا
لا خطأ في هذا الاعتقاد
هذا اعتقاد صحيح عند جميع الناس
questions.answer: لا شيء يخلد الإنسان في الدنيا، والمال لا ينفعه يوم القيامة

stages.title: Al-Humazah (III) — Al-Hutamah
stages.description: The Crusher — a name of the Hellfire and its severity

questions.text: "كَلَّا لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ" — what does "الحطمة" mean?
options: The Crusher, a name of the Hellfire that crushes/breaks whatever is thrown into it
A garden in Paradise
A mountain in Makkah
A river on Earth
questions.answer: The Crusher, a name of the Hellfire that crushes/breaks whatever is thrown into it

questions.text: "وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ" is a rhetorical device used in the Qur'an to:
options: Emphasize the terrifying, indescribable nature of what follows
Simplify a difficult concept
Introduce a joke
Confuse the listener intentionally
questions.answer: Emphasize the terrifying, indescribable nature of what follows

questions.text: "نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ" describes the Hutamah as:
options: Allah's kindled Fire
A fire made by men
A fire that eventually goes out
A cool, comfortable fire
questions.answer: Allah's kindled Fire

questions.text: What does calling it "نار الله" (Allah's Fire) emphasize?
options: Its immense severity, since it is attributed directly to Allah's power
That it is a minor punishment
That it only affects animals
That it is symbolic, not real
questions.answer: Its immense severity, since it is attributed directly to Allah's power

questions.text: How is this consequence connected to the sin described earlier in the surah?
options: It is the punishment for those who mocked others and were arrogant due to their wealth
It is unrelated to the earlier verses
It is a reward for patience
It only applies to prophets who disobeyed
questions.answer: It is the punishment for those who mocked others and were arrogant due to their wealth

stages.title: Al-Humazah (IV) — Reaching the Hearts
stages.description: The vivid imagery of the Fire closing in on those who are punished

questions.text: "الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ" means the Fire:
options: Rises up and reaches over the hearts
Stays far below the earth
Only touches the skin
Never actually reaches anyone
questions.answer: Rises up and reaches over the hearts

questions.text: Why does the ayah specifically mention the fire reaching the "hearts" (al-af'idah)?
options: Because the heart is the seat of one's true feelings and intentions, where the arrogance and love of wealth originated
Because the heart is physically the strongest organ
Because the ayah is only describing biology
Because it has no particular significance
questions.answer: Because the heart is the seat of one's true feelings and intentions, where the arrogance and love of wealth originated

questions.text: "إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ" means the Fire will be:
options: Closed/sealed shut over them
Open on all sides
Cool and comfortable
Temporary and brief
questions.answer: Closed/sealed shut over them

questions.text: "فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ" describes:
options: Extended columns/pillars, further sealing/trapping them
Gardens with flowing rivers
Tall trees for shade
Roads leading out of the Fire
questions.answer: Extended columns/pillars, further sealing/trapping them

questions.text: What is the overall picture painted in the final ayat of Al-Humazah?
options: Complete entrapment with no escape, as punishment for the arrogance shown in life
A temporary punishment followed by quick release
A description of worldly wealth
A depiction of Paradise's blessings
questions.answer: Complete entrapment with no escape, as punishment for the arrogance shown in life

stages.title: Al-Humazah (V) — Lessons
stages.description: What this surah teaches about the tongue, wealth, and the heart

questions.text: What are the two major sins condemned throughout Surah Al-Humazah?
options: Backbiting/slandering others, and obsessive love & hoarding of wealth
Lying and stealing
Pride and laziness
Disbelief and idol worship
questions.answer: Backbiting/slandering others, and obsessive love & hoarding of wealth

questions.text: What does this surah teach about the purpose of wealth?
options: Wealth is not a means of eternal security; it should be used responsibly, not hoarded arrogantly
Wealth should never be earned
Wealth automatically corrupts anyone who has it
Wealth guarantees a person's salvation
questions.answer: Wealth is not a means of eternal security; it should be used responsibly, not hoarded arrogantly

questions.text: How can a believer protect themselves from the sin of humzah/lumzah?
options: By guarding the tongue, avoiding mockery/backbiting, and having good manners with all people
By avoiding all social interaction entirely
By only speaking to the wealthy
By never earning any wealth
questions.answer: By guarding the tongue, avoiding mockery/backbiting, and having good manners with all people

questions.text: How does the vivid imagery of the Hutamah connect to the surah's opening warning?
options: It shows the real consequence awaiting those who habitually mock and hoard wealth, matching the crime to the punishment
It has no relation to the opening verses
It only describes a natural disaster
It describes a reward for the wealthy
questions.answer: It shows the real consequence awaiting those who habitually mock and hoard wealth, matching the crime to the punishment

questions.text: True or False: Surah Al-Humazah only condemns wealthy people in general, without pointing to any specific behavior.
options: False
True
questions.answer: False

difficulties.label: Intermediate
difficulties.description: Stories and character — Al-Fil, Quraysh, Al-Ma'un, Al-Kawthar & Al-Kafirun

stages.title: Al-Fil (I) — The Year of the Elephant
stages.description: The story of Abraha's march on the Ka'bah

questions.text: What historical event does Surah Al-Fil refer to?
options: Abraha's attempt to destroy the Ka'bah with an army that included elephants
The Battle of Badr
The migration to Madinah
The building of the Ka'bah by Ibrahim
questions.answer: Abraha's attempt to destroy the Ka'bah with an army that included elephants

questions.text: In what year, relative to the Prophet's ﷺ birth, did the Year of the Elephant occur?
options: The same year the Prophet ﷺ was born (or shortly before)
Ten years after the Prophet's ﷺ birth
During the Prophet's ﷺ old age
A century before Islam
questions.answer: The same year the Prophet ﷺ was born (or shortly before)

questions.text: Why did Abraha march towards Makkah?
options: To destroy the Ka'bah, after building a grand church in Yemen that failed to divert Arab pilgrims
To trade with Quraysh
To convert to the religion of the Arabs
To visit relatives
questions.answer: To destroy the Ka'bah, after building a grand church in Yemen that failed to divert Arab pilgrims

questions.text: "أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ" — what does this opening rhetorical question do?
options: It draws attention to a well-known event as a sign of Allah's power
It asks the Prophet ﷺ a question he cannot answer
It denies that the event ever happened
It introduces a legal ruling
questions.answer: It draws attention to a well-known event as a sign of Allah's power

questions.text: مَن هو أبرهة؟
options: قائد جيش أراد هدم الكعبة ومعه الفيلة
أحد الصحابة
ملك من ملوك مكة
أحد أنبياء بني إسرائيل
questions.answer: قائد جيش أراد هدم الكعبة ومعه الفيلة

stages.title: Al-Fil (II) — Allah Foils Their Plan
stages.description: How Allah made the plot of the People of the Elephant fail

questions.text: "أَصْحَابِ الْفِيلِ" refers to:
options: The People/Companions of the Elephant (Abraha's army)
The people of Madinah
The tribe of Quraysh
The angels sent to help the Prophet ﷺ
questions.answer: The People/Companions of the Elephant (Abraha's army)

questions.text: "أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ" means Allah:
options: Made their plan go astray/into ruin, causing it to fail completely
Rewarded their plan with success
Ignored their plan entirely
Delayed their plan for years
questions.answer: Made their plan go astray/into ruin, causing it to fail completely

questions.text: What is emphasized by beginning the surah with a rhetorical question about something well known?
options: The certainty and undeniable nature of this sign of Allah's power
That the event is only a legend
That no one had heard of this event before
That the event is unimportant
questions.answer: The certainty and undeniable nature of this sign of Allah's power

questions.text: What general lesson does this opening teach about those who oppose Allah's sacred symbols?
options: Their plots ultimately fail no matter how powerful they seem
They always succeed in the end
Allah never intervenes in worldly affairs
Only prophets are protected from such plots
questions.answer: Their plots ultimately fail no matter how powerful they seem

questions.text: ماذا فعل الله بكيد أصحاب الفيل؟
options: جعله في تضليل، أي أبطله وأفشله
قبله ونصرهم
أجّله إلى وقت آخر
لم يتدخل فيه
questions.answer: جعله في تضليل، أي أبطله وأفشله

stages.title: Al-Fil (III) — The Ababil Birds
stages.description: Allah's small but decisive means of destroying a mighty army

questions.text: "طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ" refers to:
options: Flocks of birds sent by Allah against Abraha's army
A type of storm cloud
A group of angels in human form
A tribe that helped Quraysh
questions.answer: Flocks of birds sent by Allah against Abraha's army

questions.text: "تَرْمِيهِمْ بِحِجَارَةٍ مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ" means the birds threw at them:
options: Stones of baked clay
Arrows of fire
Handfuls of sand
Pieces of wood
questions.answer: Stones of baked clay

questions.text: What miraculous element does this event show about Allah's support for the sacred House?
options: Allah defended the Ka'bah using a small, seemingly weak means (birds) against a mighty army
Allah needed the help of the Quraysh army
Allah used a natural disease outbreak only
Allah allowed the Ka'bah to be destroyed first
questions.answer: Allah defended the Ka'bah using a small, seemingly weak means (birds) against a mighty army

questions.text: من الذي أرسل الطير الأبابيل؟
options: الله سبحانه وتعالى
أهل مكة
أبرهة نفسه
جبريل عليه السلام وحده بدون أمر
questions.answer: الله سبحانه وتعالى

questions.text: Why is it significant that Allah used something as small as birds and stones rather than a human army?
options: It shows His absolute power — He needs no conventional means to defeat the mightiest forces
It shows that Allah's power is limited to small creatures
It shows the birds were naturally stronger than elephants
It has no particular significance
questions.answer: It shows His absolute power — He needs no conventional means to defeat the mightiest forces

stages.title: Al-Fil (IV) — Like Eaten Straw
stages.description: The complete devastation of Abraha's army

questions.text: "فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ" means Allah made them like:
options: Straw/chaff that has been eaten (completely devastated)
A garden in full bloom
Fresh green crops
A calm sea
questions.answer: Straw/chaff that has been eaten (completely devastated)

questions.text: What does this simile emphasize about the fate of Abraha's army?
options: Total destruction, as if they were consumed and left as worthless remains
A partial and temporary setback
Their eventual victory over Makkah
Their peaceful retreat
questions.answer: Total destruction, as if they were consumed and left as worthless remains

questions.text: عصف مأكول - لماذا شُبِّه الجيش بهذا؟
options: للدلالة على شدة الهلاك والدمار الذي أصابهم
للدلالة على قوتهم الباقية
للدلالة على نجاتهم
لا علاقة لهذا التشبيه بمصيرهم
questions.answer: للدلالة على شدة الهلاك والدمار الذي أصابهم

questions.text: What does this ending teach about the outcome for those who transgress against Allah's sanctities?
options: Complete ruin and humiliation, regardless of their apparent strength
Eventual forgiveness without consequence
A delayed punishment in the next life only
No punishment at all in most cases
questions.answer: Complete ruin and humiliation, regardless of their apparent strength

questions.text: How does the brevity of this surah's destruction narrative (only 5 ayat) reflect the ease of Allah's power?
options: It shows that for Allah, destroying even a mighty army takes no great effort
It shows the event was insignificant
It shows the story is incomplete
It shows Allah struggled to defeat them
questions.answer: It shows that for Allah, destroying even a mighty army takes no great effort

stages.title: Al-Fil (V) — Lessons
stages.description: What this surah teaches about Allah's protection of His sacred House

questions.text: What is the primary lesson of Surah Al-Fil regarding the Ka'bah?
options: Allah Himself protects His sacred House, no matter how powerful the aggressor
The Ka'bah was left undefended by Allah
The Ka'bah was destroyed and later rebuilt
The Ka'bah has no special status in Islam
questions.answer: Allah Himself protects His sacred House, no matter how powerful the aggressor

questions.text: How does this surah connect historically to the Prophet's ﷺ birth?
options: It occurred the same year, showing Allah's providence was already preparing the way for the final Messenger
It occurred a thousand years before the Prophet ﷺ
It has no connection to his birth at all
It occurred after his death
questions.answer: It occurred the same year, showing Allah's providence was already preparing the way for the final Messenger

questions.text: What does this surah teach about relying on worldly power versus Allah's support?
options: Worldly power (armies, elephants) is nothing next to Allah's decree
Worldly power always defeats divine intervention
Allah only supports the wealthy
Worldly power is irrelevant to faith entirely
questions.answer: Worldly power (armies, elephants) is nothing next to Allah's decree

questions.text: Why is this surah often mentioned alongside Surah Quraysh?
options: Because Quraysh's safety and trade were a direct blessing that followed from Allah's protection of the Ka'bah
Because they share the exact same wording
Because they were revealed on the same day for unrelated reasons
Because both mention Abraha by name
questions.answer: Because Quraysh's safety and trade were a direct blessing that followed from Allah's protection of the Ka'bah

questions.text: True or False: Abraha succeeded in partially damaging the Ka'bah before being stopped.
options: False
True
questions.answer: False

stages.title: Surah Quraysh (I) — Ilaf & the Link to Al-Fil
stages.description: The meaning of Ilaf and how this surah connects to Al-Fil

questions.text: "لِإِيلَافِ قُرَيْشٍ" — what does "الإيلاف" mean?
options: Familiarity/security, referring to the secure arrangement Quraysh had for their trade journeys
A type of trade good
A name for the Ka'bah
A tribal war
questions.answer: Familiarity/security, referring to the secure arrangement Quraysh had for their trade journeys

questions.text: Why do many scholars link Surah Quraysh directly to Surah Al-Fil?
options: Because the outcome of Al-Fil (Allah's protection of the Ka'bah) is what allowed Quraysh to remain secure and continue their trade
Because they were revealed to different prophets
Because they describe unrelated historical events
Because Quraysh is mentioned by name in Al-Fil
questions.answer: Because the outcome of Al-Fil (Allah's protection of the Ka'bah) is what allowed Quraysh to remain secure and continue their trade

questions.text: What tribe is specifically referred to in this surah?
options: Quraysh, the tribe of the Prophet ﷺ and custodians of the Ka'bah
The tribe of Thaqif
The tribe of Aws
The tribe of Khazraj
questions.answer: Quraysh, the tribe of the Prophet ﷺ and custodians of the Ka'bah

questions.text: What broader meaning does "Ilaf" carry beyond travel?
options: A sense of being accustomed to/settled into safety and routine, granted by Allah
A type of financial debt
A form of tribal punishment
A ritual sacrifice
questions.answer: A sense of being accustomed to/settled into safety and routine, granted by Allah

questions.text: لماذا سميت السورة باسم "قريش"؟
options: لأنها تتحدث عن نعمة الله على قبيلة قريش بالإيلاف والأمن
لأن قريشا نزلت عليهم أول آية في القرآن
لأنها أطول سورة تخص قبيلة
لا سبب معروف لهذه التسمية
questions.answer: لأنها تتحدث عن نعمة الله على قبيلة قريش بالإيلاف والأمن

stages.title: Surah Quraysh (II) — The Two Journeys
stages.description: The winter and summer trade caravans of Quraysh

questions.text: "رِحْلَةَ الشِّتَاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ" refers to:
options: Quraysh's two annual trade caravans, one in winter and one in summer
Two pilgrimages made every year
Two battles fought by Quraysh
Two migrations of the Prophet ﷺ
questions.answer: Quraysh's two annual trade caravans, one in winter and one in summer

questions.text: Why were these trade journeys significant for Quraysh?
options: They were the backbone of their economy and prosperity, made possible by the safety Allah granted them
They were purely religious pilgrimages with no economic value
They were forced upon them by foreign rulers
They had no real importance to their daily life
questions.answer: They were the backbone of their economy and prosperity, made possible by the safety Allah granted them

questions.text: رحلة الشتاء كانت إلى أين؟
options: اليمن
الشام
العراق
مصر
questions.answer: اليمن

questions.text: رحلة الصيف كانت إلى أين؟
options: الشام
اليمن
الحبشة
فارس
questions.answer: الشام

questions.text: What does Allah want Quraysh, and us, to reflect on by mentioning these journeys?
options: That their safety and provision were blessings from Allah, deserving gratitude and worship
That trade is more important than worship
That travel itself is a form of worship
That Quraysh earned their safety through military strength alone
questions.answer: That their safety and provision were blessings from Allah, deserving gratitude and worship

stages.title: Surah Quraysh (III) — The Command to Worship
stages.description: Responding to Allah's favors with sincere worship

questions.text: "فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هَٰذَا الْبَيْتِ" means:
options: So let them worship the Lord of this House (the Ka'bah)
So let them visit this House once a year
So let them rebuild this House
So let them trade near this House
questions.answer: So let them worship the Lord of this House (the Ka'bah)

questions.text: What two specific favors are mentioned in the final ayah?
options: Feeding them against hunger, and securing them from fear
Giving them wealth and giving them children
Granting them victory and granting them land
Teaching them writing and teaching them trade
questions.answer: Feeding them against hunger, and securing them from fear

questions.text: "أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ" — what does this teach about the response owed for blessings?
options: Gratitude to Allah expressed through worship, since He is the true source of provision and security
That no gratitude is required for worldly blessings
That gratitude should be shown only to other people
That security and food are unrelated to Allah's favor
questions.answer: Gratitude to Allah expressed through worship, since He is the true source of provision and security

questions.text: What is the overall theme connecting Surah Al-Fil and Surah Quraysh together?
options: Allah's protection of the Ka'bah in Al-Fil led directly to the safety and prosperity described in Quraysh
They describe two completely unrelated tribes
Al-Fil promises punishment while Quraysh promises reward for the same people, unrelated to each other
They were both revealed after the Hijrah
questions.answer: Allah's protection of the Ka'bah in Al-Fil led directly to the safety and prosperity described in Quraysh

questions.text: True or False: The surah commands Quraysh to worship the Ka'bah building itself.
options: False — it commands worship of the Lord of the House, not the House itself
True — the Ka'bah itself is to be worshipped
questions.answer: False — it commands worship of the Lord of the House, not the House itself

stages.title: Al-Ma'un (I) — Denying the Judgment
stages.description: Who is the one who denies the Day of Recompense?

questions.text: "أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ" — what does "الدين" mean here?
options: The Judgment/Recompense (the Day of Reckoning)
The religion of Islam only
A financial debt
A type of worship ritual
questions.answer: The Judgment/Recompense (the Day of Reckoning)

questions.text: What does "يكذب بالدين" describe?
options: Someone who denies/disbelieves in the Day of Judgment
Someone who prays five times a day
Someone who gives charity secretly
Someone who fasts voluntarily
questions.answer: Someone who denies/disbelieves in the Day of Judgment

questions.text: How does the surah answer its own opening question about who this denier is?
options: It describes him through his actions: harshness to the orphan and neglect of feeding the poor
It names a specific person directly
It says the denier cannot be identified
It describes him as someone who prays too much
questions.answer: It describes him through his actions: harshness to the orphan and neglect of feeding the poor

questions.text: Why is it significant that disbelief in the Hereafter is defined through actions rather than statements?
options: It shows that true faith in the Judgment naturally produces compassion; lack of compassion reveals a defective belief
It shows that actions have no connection to belief
It shows that only verbal declarations matter in Islam
It shows that good deeds are irrelevant to faith
questions.answer: It shows that true faith in the Judgment naturally produces compassion; lack of compassion reveals a defective belief

questions.text: من هو "المكذب بالدين" كما وصفته السورة؟
options: من يقسو على اليتيم ولا يحض على طعام المسكين
من يصلي في المسجد دائما
من يصوم رمضان كل عام
من يحج بيت الله الحرام
questions.answer: من يقسو على اليتيم ولا يحض على طعام المسكين

stages.title: Al-Ma'un (II) — Harshness to the Orphan
stages.description: The two actions that reveal a hardened heart

questions.text: "فَذَٰلِكَ الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ" means he:
options: Repels/pushes away the orphan harshly
Adopts the orphan kindly
Feeds the orphan generously
Teaches the orphan to read
questions.answer: Repels/pushes away the orphan harshly

questions.text: "وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ" means he:
options: Does not encourage/urge feeding the poor
Personally feeds every poor person he meets
Forces others to fast
Gives all his wealth to the poor
questions.answer: Does not encourage/urge feeding the poor

questions.text: Why does the ayah say "does not urge" rather than simply "does not feed"?
options: To show that even failing to encourage others toward this good deed is blameworthy, not just personally withholding
Because feeding the poor is not actually required in Islam
Because urging others is worse than feeding them personally
Because the wording has no particular significance
questions.answer: To show that even failing to encourage others toward this good deed is blameworthy, not just personally withholding

questions.text: What does harshness toward orphans reveal about a person's heart, according to this surah?
options: A lack of true faith and mercy, since caring for the vulnerable is a sign of real belief
Nothing significant about their faith
That they are simply following cultural norms
That they are protecting their own wealth wisely
questions.answer: A lack of true faith and mercy, since caring for the vulnerable is a sign of real belief

questions.text: يدع اليتيم - ماذا تعني هذه الكلمة؟
options: يدفعه ويطرده بجفاء وقسوة
يحتضنه برفق
يعلمه القرآن
يزوره كل يوم
questions.answer: يدفعه ويطرده بجفاء وقسوة

stages.title: Al-Ma'un (III) — Woe to the Praying Ones
stages.description: A surprising warning aimed at those who pray

questions.text: "فَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُصَلِّينَ" — surprisingly, this warning is directed at:
options: Those who pray, but with a specific fault clarified in the next ayah
Those who never pray at all
The disbelievers of Makkah only
The angels who record deeds
questions.answer: Those who pray, but with a specific fault clarified in the next ayah

questions.text: "الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ" means they are:
options: Heedless/neglectful of their prayer
Extremely devoted to their prayer
Praying too many voluntary prayers
Unable to pray due to illness
questions.answer: Heedless/neglectful of their prayer

questions.text: Does "sahoon" (heedlessness) here mean forgetting a prayer occasionally by honest mistake?
options: No — most scholars explain it as chronic negligence, such as delaying prayers or performing them without any real concern
Yes, it refers only to a single honest mistake
Yes, and it carries no real blame at all
It refers to being distracted by beautiful recitation
questions.answer: No — most scholars explain it as chronic negligence, such as delaying prayers or performing them without any real concern

questions.text: Why is this warning so severe, given that the people described do pray?
options: Because it shows that outward ritual without sincerity, care, or consistency does not fulfill the true purpose of prayer
Because praying is itself considered a sin in this context
Because they should have prayed even more times per day
Because the warning is not actually severe at all
questions.answer: Because it shows that outward ritual without sincerity, care, or consistency does not fulfill the true purpose of prayer

questions.text: ما معنى "ساهون" عن الصلاة؟
options: غافلون عنها، لا يبالون بأدائها في وقتها أو بخشوعها
حريصون عليها جدا
يؤدونها في أول وقتها دائما
يصلونها بخشوع تام
questions.answer: غافلون عنها، لا يبالون بأدائها في وقتها أو بخشوعها

stages.title: Al-Ma'un (IV) — Showing Off
stages.description: The danger of Riya' — performing worship to be seen

questions.text: "الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ" describes people who:
options: Show off, performing good deeds to be seen by others rather than sincerely for Allah
Hide their good deeds completely from everyone
Perform deeds only in secret
Never perform any good deeds at all
questions.answer: Show off, performing good deeds to be seen by others rather than sincerely for Allah

questions.text: How does riya' (showing off) relate to the earlier description of neglecting prayer?
options: Both reveal a lack of true sincerity — one is careless in private, the other only performs to be seen in public
They are completely unrelated behaviors
Riya' is actually praised in this surah
Only one of the two behaviors is condemned
questions.answer: Both reveal a lack of true sincerity — one is careless in private, the other only performs to be seen in public

questions.text: Why is riya' considered dangerous in Islam?
options: It can nullify the reward of good deeds since sincerity (ikhlas) to Allah alone is a condition for acceptance
It has no effect on the reward of deeds
It is only a minor social faux pas
It only affects deeds done in the mosque
questions.answer: It can nullify the reward of good deeds since sincerity (ikhlas) to Allah alone is a condition for acceptance

questions.text: يراءون - ما معناها؟
options: يفعلون العبادة ليراهم الناس لا ابتغاء وجه الله
يفعلون العبادة سرا دون أن يعلم بها أحد
يتركون العبادة كليا
يخلصون العبادة لله وحده
questions.answer: يفعلون العبادة ليراهم الناس لا ابتغاء وجه الله

questions.text: What contrast does the surah draw between someone who denies the Judgment through actions and someone who prays but shows off?
options: Both share the same underlying flaw: lack of genuine concern for Allah and the Hereafter, despite outward differences
There is no connection between the two at all
The one who shows off is actually praised in comparison
Only the denier is blamed; the one showing off is excused
questions.answer: Both share the same underlying flaw: lack of genuine concern for Allah and the Hereafter, despite outward differences

stages.title: Al-Ma'un (V) — Withholding Small Kindnesses
stages.description: The final verse, and the overall lesson of the surah

questions.text: "وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ" means they:
options: Withhold even small, simple items of assistance from others
Give away all their wealth freely
Refuse to eat with others
Always lend their belongings generously
questions.answer: Withhold even small, simple items of assistance from others

questions.text: What is "al-Ma'un" generally explained as?
options: Small everyday items or acts of help neighbors commonly lend one another, or basic assistance in general
A large sum of charity money
A specific type of prayer
A pilgrimage ritual
questions.answer: Small everyday items or acts of help neighbors commonly lend one another, or basic assistance in general

questions.text: Why does the surah end on withholding something so small?
options: To show the depth of a stingy, uncaring heart — if someone won't even give small easy kindnesses, their claim to faith is hollow
Because small matters are the most important part of religion
Because it has no real significance
Because it contradicts everything said earlier in the surah
questions.answer: To show the depth of a stingy, uncaring heart — if someone won't even give small easy kindnesses, their claim to faith is hollow

questions.text: What is the central theme uniting the entire Surah Al-Ma'un?
options: True faith in the Hereafter must show itself through sincere worship and genuine compassion toward others
Wealth is forbidden in Islam
Only formal prayer matters, not compassion
The Hereafter has no connection to worldly behavior
questions.answer: True faith in the Hereafter must show itself through sincere worship and genuine compassion toward others

questions.text: What practical lesson can a believer take from this surah in daily life?
options: To care for orphans and the poor, pray with sincerity and attentiveness, and be generous even in small matters
To avoid praying in congregation
To focus only on personal wealth accumulation
To avoid helping others to prevent showing off
questions.answer: To care for orphans and the poor, pray with sincerity and attentiveness, and be generous even in small matters

stages.title: Al-Kawthar (I) — Abundant Good
stages.description: The meaning of Al-Kawthar and why the surah was revealed

questions.text: "إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ" — what does "الكوثر" mean?
options: Abundant good; most commonly explained as a river/fountain in Paradise given to the Prophet ﷺ
A type of prayer performed only at night
A tribal alliance
A famous well in Madinah
questions.answer: Abundant good; most commonly explained as a river/fountain in Paradise given to the Prophet ﷺ

questions.text: Why was this surah revealed?
options: As comfort to the Prophet ﷺ after some disbelievers mocked him for having no surviving sons, calling him 'abtar'
To command the Hajj rituals
To warn against a specific enemy tribe
To describe the Day of Judgment in detail
questions.answer: As comfort to the Prophet ﷺ after some disbelievers mocked him for having no surviving sons, calling him 'abtar'

questions.text: What does "Al-Kawthar" also represent beyond the specific river, according to some scholars?
options: All the abundant good Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ, including prophethood, honor, and his intercession
Only his wealth in this world
Only his tribal status
Only his physical strength
questions.answer: All the abundant good Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ, including prophethood, honor, and his intercession

questions.text: من الذي أعطى النبي ﷺ الكوثر؟
options: الله سبحانه وتعالى
جبريل عليه السلام من عنده
أحد الصحابة
أهل مكة
questions.answer: الله سبحانه وتعالى

questions.text: What does the surah's opening word "إِنَّا" (We) emphasize?
options: The majesty and certainty of the gift, given directly and emphatically by Allah
That the gift is uncertain and conditional
That the gift comes from multiple sources
That the gift was small and insignificant
questions.answer: The majesty and certainty of the gift, given directly and emphatically by Allah

stages.title: Al-Kawthar (II) — Prayer & Sacrifice
stages.description: The grateful response commanded after receiving Al-Kawthar

questions.text: "فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ" — what two acts of worship are commanded here?
options: Prayer (Salah) and sacrifice (Nahr)
Fasting and charity
Hajj and Umrah
Reciting Qur'an and giving da'wah
questions.answer: Prayer (Salah) and sacrifice (Nahr)

questions.text: Why are these two acts commanded as a response to receiving Al-Kawthar?
options: As a form of gratitude — responding to Allah's abundant blessing with sincere worship directed to Him alone
Because they are unrelated obligations mentioned by coincidence
Because they replace the need for any other worship
Because they were only meant for a single occasion
questions.answer: As a form of gratitude — responding to Allah's abundant blessing with sincere worship directed to Him alone

questions.text: What is significant about pairing prayer (a physical act of worship) with sacrifice (an act often tied to wealth)?
options: It combines devotion of both body and wealth as complete gratitude to Allah
It shows that only wealthy people can properly worship Allah
It shows prayer and sacrifice contradict each other
It has no particular significance
questions.answer: It combines devotion of both body and wealth as complete gratitude to Allah

questions.text: صلِّ لربك وانحر - لمن يكون النحر (الذبح)؟
options: لله وحده لا لغيره
للأصنام كما كان يفعل المشركون
لأي جهة يريدها الإنسان
لا يشترط توجيهه لأحد
questions.answer: لله وحده لا لغيره

questions.text: What does this ayah teach about the connection between blessings and worship?
options: True gratitude for Allah's blessings should be expressed through dedicated worship directed only to Him
Blessings have no connection to how one worships
Worship should decrease as blessings increase
Gratitude should be shown to people, never to Allah
questions.answer: True gratitude for Allah's blessings should be expressed through dedicated worship directed only to Him

stages.title: Al-Kawthar (III) — The One Who Is Cut Off
stages.description: How history proved the mockers wrong

questions.text: "إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ الْأَبْتَرُ" means:
options: Indeed, it is your enemy/hater who is cut off, without lasting legacy
Indeed, you yourself are cut off
Indeed, your enemy will be forgiven
Indeed, your enemy will become wealthy
questions.answer: Indeed, it is your enemy/hater who is cut off, without lasting legacy

questions.text: Who was this ayah originally addressing?
options: Those who mocked the Prophet ﷺ for lacking male heirs, implying his message would die out with him
The believers of Madinah
The angels who record deeds
A specific king of Persia
questions.answer: Those who mocked the Prophet ﷺ for lacking male heirs, implying his message would die out with him

questions.text: How did history prove this ayah true?
options: The Prophet's ﷺ message, legacy, and Ummah flourished and spread worldwide, while his mockers' names and legacies faded
The Prophet's ﷺ message disappeared within a generation
Neither side left any historical legacy
The mockers' descendants ruled the Muslim world
questions.answer: The Prophet's ﷺ message, legacy, and Ummah flourished and spread worldwide, while his mockers' names and legacies faded

questions.text: الأبتر - من هو حقيقة كما بينت السورة؟
options: عدو النبي ﷺ ومن يبغضه، لا النبي نفسه
النبي ﷺ نفسه
أبو بكر الصديق
جميع أهل مكة بلا استثناء
questions.answer: عدو النبي ﷺ ومن يبغضه، لا النبي نفسه

questions.text: What is the overall lesson of Surah Al-Kawthar regarding worldly mockery of the righteous?
options: Allah defends and honors His close servants, and their true legacy endures despite the taunts of their enemies
Mockery always succeeds in damaging a person's legacy
Allah is indifferent to how His servants are treated
Legacy is determined by wealth alone
questions.answer: Allah defends and honors His close servants, and their true legacy endures despite the taunts of their enemies

stages.title: Al-Kafirun (I) — Occasion of Revelation
stages.description: The compromise offered to the Prophet ﷺ, and his firm rejection

questions.text: What compromise did the disbelievers of Quraysh offer the Prophet ﷺ, prompting this surah?
options: That he worship their gods for a year in exchange for them worshipping Allah for a year
That he leave Makkah peacefully forever
That he marry into their tribe
That he stop preaching only in public
questions.answer: That he worship their gods for a year in exchange for them worshipping Allah for a year

questions.text: What was the Prophet's ﷺ response, as reflected in this surah?
options: A firm and complete rejection of any compromise in worship
A partial agreement to their terms
Silence and no response at all
A request for more time to decide
questions.answer: A firm and complete rejection of any compromise in worship

questions.text: What core principle does this surah establish about matters of faith?
options: There can be no mixing or compromise between Tawhid and shirk
All forms of worship are equally acceptable
Compromise is always the best solution in religion
Faith should adapt to social pressure
questions.answer: There can be no mixing or compromise between Tawhid and shirk

questions.text: لماذا نزلت سورة الكافرون؟
options: ردا على عرض كفار قريش بالمهادنة في العبادة مع النبي ﷺ
بمناسبة فتح مكة
بمناسبة غزوة بدر
بمناسبة وفاة أبي طالب
questions.answer: ردا على عرض كفار قريش بالمهادنة في العبادة مع النبي ﷺ

questions.text: This surah is sometimes traditionally called "Al-Muqashqishah," meaning:
options: The one that cleanses/frees one from shirk
The one that describes Paradise
The one revealed at night
The one about trade journeys
questions.answer: The one that cleanses/frees one from shirk

stages.title: Al-Kafirun (II) — No Worship in Common
stages.description: The opening declaration of complete separation in worship

questions.text: "قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ" begins with a command to the Prophet ﷺ to:
options: Say/declare directly to the disbelievers
Remain silent before the disbelievers
Write a letter to the disbelievers
Ask the angels to intervene
questions.answer: Say/declare directly to the disbelievers

questions.text: "لَا أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ" means:
options: I do not worship what you worship
I worship exactly what you worship
I will worship your gods for one year
I do not worship at all
questions.answer: I do not worship what you worship

questions.text: "وَلَا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ" means:
options: Nor do you worship what I worship
You worship exactly what I worship
You will soon worship what I worship
Neither of us worships anything
questions.answer: Nor do you worship what I worship

questions.text: What is being firmly established in these opening declarations?
options: A clear, total distinction between the worship of the believer and that of the disbeliever, with no overlap
That both sides actually worship the same god under different names
That worship does not matter in the end
That the Prophet ﷺ was open to changing his practice
questions.answer: A clear, total distinction between the worship of the believer and that of the disbeliever, with no overlap

questions.text: لا أعبد ما تعبدون - ماذا تدل هذه الجملة؟
options: البراءة التامة من عبادة الأصنام
الموافقة على عبادة الأصنام مؤقتا
الشك في التوحيد
طلب المهادنة مع الكفار
questions.answer: البراءة التامة من عبادة الأصنام

stages.title: Al-Kafirun (III) — Repetition for Emphasis
stages.description: Why the surah restates its rejection a second time

questions.text: Ayaat 4-5 repeat similar meanings to ayaat 2-3. Why does the surah repeat itself?
options: For strong emphasis, to remove any doubt of compromise both in the past and future
By accidental scribal error
Because the first statement was considered invalid
To make the surah longer for recitation purposes only
questions.answer: For strong emphasis, to remove any doubt of compromise both in the past and future

questions.text: What does the repeated denial teach about firmness in faith?
options: A believer's rejection of falsehood should be firm, clear, and unwavering — not open to negotiation
A believer should always seek middle ground on matters of creed
Repetition shows weakness in one's argument
Firmness in faith is unnecessary
questions.answer: A believer's rejection of falsehood should be firm, clear, and unwavering — not open to negotiation

questions.text: ولا أنا عابد ما عبدتم - ماذا تكرر هذه الآية؟
options: تأكيد البراءة من عبادة الأصنام مرة أخرى
الموافقة على عبادة الأصنام
طلب الصلح مع الكفار
التراجع عن الدعوة
questions.answer: تأكيد البراءة من عبادة الأصنام مرة أخرى

questions.text: Why might repetition be a particularly powerful rhetorical tool in this surah?
options: Repetition reinforces the message with unmistakable clarity and finality, leaving no room for compromise
Repetition confuses the listener intentionally
Repetition is a sign of uncertainty in the message
Repetition weakens the emphasis of the message
questions.answer: Repetition reinforces the message with unmistakable clarity and finality, leaving no room for compromise

questions.text: What subtle nuance do many commentators note about the phrasing used in the repeated verses compared to the first set?
options: A slight difference emphasizing the settled, habitual nature of each side's worship, reinforcing permanence of the separation
There is absolutely no linguistic difference of any kind between them
The repeated verses are grammatically incorrect
The repeated verses refer to a different group of people entirely
questions.answer: A slight difference emphasizing the settled, habitual nature of each side's worship, reinforcing permanence of the separation

stages.title: Al-Kafirun (IV) — Lakum Deenukum & Lessons
stages.description: The closing verse and its meaning for coexistence without compromise

questions.text: "لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ" means:
options: For you is your religion, and for me is my religion
Your religion and mine are identical
You must abandon your religion immediately
Religion does not matter at all
questions.answer: For you is your religion, and for me is my religion

questions.text: Does this final ayah mean Islam accepts all religions as equally valid paths to truth?
options: No — it establishes peaceful coexistence and non-compulsion in belief, not equal validity
Yes, it declares all religions equally true
Yes, it cancels the concept of Tawhid entirely
It has no relevance to interfaith relations at all
questions.answer: No — it establishes peaceful coexistence and non-compulsion in belief, not equal validity

questions.text: What principle from Islamic teaching does this ayah support?
options: 'There is no compulsion in religion' — freedom of belief, without forcing conversion
That force should always be used to convert others
That religion is a private matter of no consequence
That all forms of worship must eventually be unified
questions.answer: 'There is no compulsion in religion' — freedom of belief, without forcing conversion

questions.text: What is the overall lesson of Surah Al-Kafirun regarding Tawhid and compromise?
options: A believer must never compromise the core of their faith for worldly gain or social pressure, while still dealing justly and peacefully with others
A believer should compromise their faith whenever it is socially convenient
Tawhid is negotiable in certain circumstances
Peaceful coexistence requires abandoning one's own beliefs
questions.answer: A believer must never compromise the core of their faith for worldly gain or social pressure, while still dealing justly and peacefully with others

questions.text: True or False: This surah teaches that Muslims should never interact peacefully with non-Muslims.
options: False
True
questions.answer: False

difficulties.label: Advanced
difficulties.description: Victory, Tawhid & protection — An-Nasr, Al-Masad, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas & review

stages.title: An-Nasr (I) — Victory and a Sign
stages.description: The Conquest of Makkah and what it signaled to the Prophet ﷺ

questions.text: "إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ" — what historical event does "al-Fath" primarily refer to?
options: The Conquest of Makkah (Fath Makkah)
The Battle of Uhud
The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
The Farewell Pilgrimage
questions.answer: The Conquest of Makkah (Fath Makkah)

questions.text: This surah is traditionally understood by many companions, like Ibn 'Abbas, as a sign of what?
options: The nearing of the Prophet's ﷺ death, informing him his mission was complete
The start of the Prophet's ﷺ mission
An upcoming military defeat
The revelation of the first verse of the Qur'an
questions.answer: The nearing of the Prophet's ﷺ death, informing him his mission was complete

questions.text: What does it mean that this surah signals completion of the message rather than just military victory?
options: It shows that the ultimate goal was the spread of Islam and people entering it, which had now been achieved widely
It shows the Prophet ﷺ had failed in his mission
It shows the message was only meant for Makkah
It shows military conquest was the sole purpose of his mission
questions.answer: It shows that the ultimate goal was the spread of Islam and people entering it, which had now been achieved widely

questions.text: متى نزلت سورة النصر تقريبا؟
options: بعد فتح مكة، قرب نهاية حياة النبي ﷺ
في بداية الدعوة بمكة
بعد غزوة بدر مباشرة
قبل الهجرة إلى المدينة
questions.answer: بعد فتح مكة، قرب نهاية حياة النبي ﷺ

questions.text: How did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) reportedly understand this surah when asked among the companions?
options: As an indication of the Prophet's ﷺ approaching death and the completion of his mission
As a command to fight more battles
As permission to leave Makkah
As a description of Paradise
questions.answer: As an indication of the Prophet's ﷺ approaching death and the completion of his mission

stages.title: An-Nasr (II) — Multitudes Enter Islam
stages.description: The fruit of decades of patient da'wah

questions.text: "وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا" means people entered Islam:
options: In multitudes/crowds (groups after groups)
One person at a time, very rarely
Only after the Prophet's ﷺ death
Through forced conversion
questions.answer: In multitudes/crowds (groups after groups)

questions.text: Before the Conquest of Makkah, how did people typically enter Islam, in contrast to "afwaja"?
options: Individually or in small numbers, often facing hardship
Always in massive tribal groups
Only through royal decree
Through inheritance from their parents automatically
questions.answer: Individually or in small numbers, often facing hardship

questions.text: What changed after the Conquest of Makkah that led to mass conversions?
options: The removal of the main political/tribal obstacle (Quraysh's dominance) opened the way for entire tribes to accept Islam freely
A new prophet was sent to convince them
Trade routes were closed, forcing people to convert
The Ka'bah was destroyed and rebuilt as a mosque
questions.answer: The removal of the main political/tribal obstacle (Quraysh's dominance) opened the way for entire tribes to accept Islam freely

questions.text: أفواجا - ماذا تعني هذه الكلمة؟
options: جماعات كثيرة متتابعة
شخص واحد فقط
عدد قليل جدا
قبيلة واحدة فقط
questions.answer: جماعات كثيرة متتابعة

questions.text: What does this ayah show about the fruit of the Prophet's ﷺ decades of struggle?
options: The patient effort of dawah finally led to widespread, large-scale acceptance of the truth
His efforts ultimately failed to convince anyone
Only his close family ever accepted Islam
Mass conversion happened without any prior effort
questions.answer: The patient effort of dawah finally led to widespread, large-scale acceptance of the truth

stages.title: An-Nasr (III) — Glorify & Seek Forgiveness
stages.description: How a believer should respond to success and victory

questions.text: "فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ" commands the Prophet ﷺ to do what upon witnessing this victory?
options: Glorify Allah with praise, and seek His forgiveness
Celebrate publicly with feasting
Punish his former enemies harshly
Retire from preaching immediately
questions.answer: Glorify Allah with praise, and seek His forgiveness

questions.text: Why command seeking forgiveness (istighfar) at the peak of success and victory?
options: To teach humility — success is never a moment for pride but for gratitude and returning to Allah
Because the Prophet ﷺ had committed a major sin
Because victory itself is a form of wrongdoing
Because istighfar has no real connection to success
questions.answer: To teach humility — success is never a moment for pride but for gratitude and returning to Allah

questions.text: "إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّابًا" describes Allah as:
options: The One who constantly accepts repentance
The One who never forgives
The One who only forgives prophets
The One who delays forgiveness for years
questions.answer: The One who constantly accepts repentance

questions.text: فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره - ما الدرس المستفاد عند النصر؟
options: شكر الله والتواضع له والإكثار من الاستغفار
الافتخار بالنصر أمام الناس
نسيان الله بعد تحقيق النجاح
الانتقام من كل من عارضه سابقا
questions.answer: شكر الله والتواضع له والإكثار من الاستغفار

questions.text: What overall lesson does Surah An-Nasr give believers about handling success?
options: To respond to victory and blessings with humility, gratitude, and turning back to Allah, not arrogance
To take full personal credit for any success achieved
To stop worshipping once success is achieved
To view success as a sign that no more effort is needed
questions.answer: To respond to victory and blessings with humility, gratitude, and turning back to Allah, not arrogance

stages.title: Al-Masad (I) — Abu Lahab at Safa
stages.description: The incident that prompted this surah's revelation

questions.text: What incident prompted the revelation of Surah Al-Masad?
options: Abu Lahab publicly mocking and rejecting the Prophet ﷺ after he called his family to Islam from Mount Safa
Abu Lahab accepting Islam secretly
Abu Lahab's death in battle
Abu Lahab's migration to Madinah
questions.answer: Abu Lahab publicly mocking and rejecting the Prophet ﷺ after he called his family to Islam from Mount Safa

questions.text: "تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ" means:
options: May the hands of Abu Lahab perish, and he has perished
May the hands of Abu Lahab be blessed
Abu Lahab will be forgiven
Abu Lahab will find great wealth
questions.answer: May the hands of Abu Lahab perish, and he has perished

questions.text: Who was Abu Lahab in relation to the Prophet ﷺ?
options: His paternal uncle, and one of his fiercest enemies
His maternal uncle who supported him
A companion who later became a scholar
A ruler of Yemen
questions.answer: His paternal uncle, and one of his fiercest enemies

questions.text: أبو لهب - لماذا سمي بهذا اللقب، بحسب أشهر الأقوال؟
options: لاحمرار وجهه وإشراقه (لهب = شعلة نار)
لأنه كان تاجرا للحطب
لأنه كان يحب النار في بيته
لأنه كان يعمل حدادا
questions.answer: لاحمرار وجهه وإشراقه (لهب = شعلة نار)

questions.text: This is one of the few surahs that names a specific individual condemned by name. What does this show about revelation?
options: Allah's knowledge of the unseen is absolute — declaring Abu Lahab's fate as a disbeliever even before his death confirmed it
It shows the Qur'an was written by the Prophet ﷺ based on personal grievances
It shows every enemy of the Prophet ﷺ is named in the Qur'an
It has no particular significance
questions.answer: Allah's knowledge of the unseen is absolute — declaring Abu Lahab's fate as a disbeliever even before his death confirmed it

stages.title: Al-Masad (II) — Wealth Won't Avail Him
stages.description: The refutation of relying on wealth and status

questions.text: "مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ" means:
options: His wealth and what he earned did not avail/benefit him at all
His wealth saved him from every hardship
He gave away all his wealth in charity
His wealth was taken by force
