questions.answer: His wealth and what he earned did not avail/benefit him at all

questions.text: What specific idea about wealth and status does this ayah refute, similar to Al-Humazah?
options: That wealth and worldly achievements can save a person from Allah's punishment or grant them immunity
That wealth should never be earned honestly
That poverty is always better than wealth
That wealth has no connection to a person's actions at all
questions.answer: That wealth and worldly achievements can save a person from Allah's punishment or grant them immunity

questions.text: What might "وَمَا كَسَبَ" (what he earned) refer to besides his wealth, according to some tafsir?
options: His children/offspring, who he saw as further support and status
His farmland only
His weapons only
His trade caravans only
questions.answer: His children/offspring, who he saw as further support and status

questions.text: ما أغنى عنه ماله - ما الدرس هنا؟
options: أن المال لا ينفع صاحبه أمام عذاب الله إذا كفر
أن المال ينفع صاحبه دائما مهما فعل
أن الفقر أفضل من العمل بأي حال
أن كسب المال محرم في الإسلام
questions.answer: أن المال لا ينفع صاحبه أمام عذاب الله إذا كفر

questions.text: How does this ayah connect to Abu Lahab's public status and pride in Makkah?
options: It shows that despite his wealth and prestige, none of it protected him from the consequences of rejecting the truth
It shows his wealth eventually saved him
It shows he had no wealth or status at all
It has no connection to his social standing
questions.answer: It shows that despite his wealth and prestige, none of it protected him from the consequences of rejecting the truth

stages.title: Al-Masad (III) — The Fire & His Wife
stages.description: The punishment awaiting Abu Lahab and his wife's role

questions.text: "سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ" means he will:
options: Burn in a flaming fire
Be rewarded with Paradise
Be forgiven completely
Live a long, peaceful life
questions.answer: Burn in a flaming fire

questions.text: "وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ" describes Abu Lahab's wife as:
options: The carrier of firewood
A generous woman
A believer who repented
A poet of Quraysh
questions.answer: The carrier of firewood

questions.text: What is the metaphorical meaning of "carrier of firewood" according to most commentators?
options: A reference to her spreading slander/gossip and stirring enmity against the Prophet ﷺ, in addition to literally placing thorns on his path
A reference to her working as a professional wood seller
A reference to her cooking skills
A reference to her wealth in property
questions.answer: A reference to her spreading slander/gossip and stirring enmity against the Prophet ﷺ, in addition to literally placing thorns on his path

questions.text: Who was Abu Lahab's wife, historically?
options: Umm Jamil (Arwa bint Harb), sister of Abu Sufyan
Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
Hind bint Utbah
Fatimah bint Al-Khattab
questions.answer: Umm Jamil (Arwa bint Harb), sister of Abu Sufyan

questions.text: حمالة الحطب - ماذا يرمز هذا الوصف؟
options: نقل الغيبة والنميمة والإفساد بين الناس
بيع الحطب في السوق
جمع الحطب لأجل الفقراء
الزراعة في مكة
questions.answer: نقل الغيبة والنميمة والإفساد بين الناس

stages.title: Al-Masad (IV) — The Rope & Lessons
stages.description: Divine justice fitting the punishment to the deed

questions.text: "فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ" means around her neck will be:
options: A rope of twisted palm fiber
A necklace of gold
A garland of flowers
Nothing at all
questions.answer: A rope of twisted palm fiber

questions.text: What is the significance of this specific, humiliating punishment for her?
options: It fits her crime — carrying 'loads' of slander against the Prophet ﷺ — showing divine justice matching punishment to deed
It is completely unrelated to her actions in life
It shows she will be rewarded instead
It is a punishment reserved only for men
questions.answer: It fits her crime — carrying 'loads' of slander against the Prophet ﷺ — showing divine justice matching punishment to deed

questions.text: What is the overall lesson of Surah Al-Masad about opposing the truth?
options: Fierce, prideful opposition to Allah's Messenger, even from close family, leads to disgrace and severe punishment regardless of wealth or status
Family members can never truly oppose a prophet
Wealth always protects a person from consequences
Opposition to the truth is always eventually forgiven
questions.answer: Fierce, prideful opposition to Allah's Messenger, even from close family, leads to disgrace and severe punishment regardless of wealth or status

questions.text: How does the fact that this surah was revealed while Abu Lahab was still alive strengthen its miraculous nature?
options: It publicly and specifically foretold his fate as a disbeliever, and he never disproved it by even pretending to accept Islam
It has no miraculous element since anyone could predict such a thing
Abu Lahab quickly proved the surah false by converting
The surah was only revealed after his death
questions.answer: It publicly and specifically foretold his fate as a disbeliever, and he never disproved it by even pretending to accept Islam

questions.text: True or False: Abu Lahab's family relation to the Prophet ﷺ gave him any special exemption from this warning.
options: False
True
questions.answer: False

stages.title: Al-Ikhlas (I) — Virtue & Context
stages.description: Why this short surah equals a third of the Qur'an

questions.text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is described in hadith as being equal to what portion of the Qur'an?
options: One-third of the Qur'an
One-tenth of the Qur'an
The entire Qur'an
One-half of the Qur'an
questions.answer: One-third of the Qur'an

questions.text: What prompted the revelation of this surah, according to many narrations?
options: The disbelievers/Jews asking the Prophet ﷺ to describe the lineage/nature of his Lord
A dispute over inheritance law
A question about the Hajj rituals
A request to describe Paradise
questions.answer: The disbelievers/Jews asking the Prophet ﷺ to describe the lineage/nature of his Lord

questions.text: What does "Al-Ikhlas" mean, and why is the surah named this?
options: Sincerity/purity; because it purifies one's belief in Allah's absolute Oneness, free from any partners or resemblance
Sincerity in prayer times only
A term for charity given in secret
A name unrelated to its content
questions.answer: Sincerity/purity; because it purifies one's belief in Allah's absolute Oneness, free from any partners or resemblance

questions.text: لماذا سميت سورة الإخلاص بهذا الاسم؟
options: لأنها تخلص وتنقي عقيدة التوحيد من الشرك
لأنها نزلت في يوم الجمعة
لأنها تتحدث عن الإخلاص في العمل فقط
لا سبب معروف لهذه التسمية
questions.answer: لأنها تخلص وتنقي عقيدة التوحيد من الشرك

questions.text: How many ayat does Surah Al-Ikhlas contain?
options: Four
Seven
Ten
Two
questions.answer: Four

stages.title: Al-Ikhlas (II) — Allahu Ahad
stages.description: The absolute, indivisible uniqueness of Allah

questions.text: "قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ" means:
options: Say: He is Allah, the One (Unique)
Say: He is Allah, the Merciful
Say: He is Allah, the Creator
Say: He is Allah, the Forgiving
questions.answer: Say: He is Allah, the One (Unique)

questions.text: What is the difference in meaning between "Ahad" (used here) and "Wahid" (also meaning 'one')?
options: 'Ahad' emphasizes absolute, indivisible uniqueness with no like or partner in any respect, more emphatic than a simple numerical 'one'
There is no difference at all between the two words
'Wahid' is more emphatic than 'Ahad'
'Ahad' means 'first' while 'Wahid' means 'unique'
questions.answer: 'Ahad' emphasizes absolute, indivisible uniqueness with no like or partner in any respect, more emphatic than a simple numerical 'one'

questions.text: What core belief (Tawhid) does this first ayah establish?
options: That Allah is singularly One in His Essence, Names, Attributes, and Actions — with nothing comparable to Him
That Allah shares His essence with the angels
That Allah has multiple equal partners
That Allah's Oneness applies only to His actions, not His essence
questions.answer: That Allah is singularly One in His Essence, Names, Attributes, and Actions — with nothing comparable to Him

questions.text: أحد - لماذا لم تستخدم كلمة "واحد" هنا؟
options: لأن "أحد" أبلغ في نفي المثيل والشريك عن الله
لأن "واحد" كلمة غير عربية
لأن "أحد" أقصر في اللفظ فقط
لا فرق بين الكلمتين إطلاقا
questions.answer: لأن "أحد" أبلغ في نفي المثيل والشريك عن الله

questions.text: Why is affirming Allah's absolute Oneness the very first and central point of this surah?
options: Because Tawhid is the foundation of the entire Islamic creed, upon which everything else is built
Because it is the easiest concept to explain
Because it has no real connection to the rest of the surah
Because it was simply the order in which it was revealed, with no deeper reason
questions.answer: Because Tawhid is the foundation of the entire Islamic creed, upon which everything else is built

stages.title: Al-Ikhlas (III) — As-Samad
stages.description: The One depended upon by all, needing none

questions.text: "اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ" — what does "As-Samad" mean?
options: The One who is depended upon by all creation for their needs, while He needs nothing from anyone
The One who created only the heavens
The One who forgives all sins automatically
The One who is hidden from creation
questions.answer: The One who is depended upon by all creation for their needs, while He needs nothing from anyone

questions.text: What does calling Allah "As-Samad" tell us about His relationship with His creation?
options: Everything in creation is in constant need of Him, while He is free of any need whatsoever
Allah is dependent on His creation for sustenance
Allah and His creation are mutually dependent
As-Samad has no bearing on Allah's relationship with creation
questions.answer: Everything in creation is in constant need of Him, while He is free of any need whatsoever

questions.text: How does As-Samad relate to Allah's perfection in all His attributes?
options: Since He is the ultimate refuge for all needs, He must be perfect and complete in knowledge, power, mercy, and every attribute
It shows Allah is imperfect in some attributes
It is unrelated to His other attributes
It only refers to His physical strength
questions.answer: Since He is the ultimate refuge for all needs, He must be perfect and complete in knowledge, power, mercy, and every attribute

questions.text: الصمد - ماذا يعني بالنسبة لحاجتنا نحن؟
options: أننا محتاجون إليه في كل شيء، وهو الغني عن كل شيء
أننا مستغنون عنه تماما
أن الله محتاج إلينا كما نحتاج إليه
لا علاقة لهذا الاسم بحاجتنا
questions.answer: أننا محتاجون إليه في كل شيء، وهو الغني عن كل شيء

questions.text: Why is "As-Samad" placed directly after "Ahad" in the surah's structure?
options: After establishing His absolute uniqueness, this ayah shows the practical implication — everyone depends on this One, Unique God alone
There is no logical connection between the two ayat
As-Samad contradicts the meaning of Ahad
The order is purely coincidental with no purpose
questions.answer: After establishing His absolute uniqueness, this ayah shows the practical implication — everyone depends on this One, Unique God alone

stages.title: Al-Ikhlas (IV) — No Begetting, No Equal
stages.description: The final refutation of every form of shirk in Allah's essence

questions.text: "لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ" means:
options: He begets not, nor was He begotten
He begets many, and was begotten once
He has one child only
He was created from light
questions.answer: He begets not, nor was He begotten

questions.text: What false beliefs does this ayah directly refute?
options: Beliefs that Allah has offspring, such as claims about a divine son, or that He was born from something/someone
Beliefs about the Day of Judgment
Beliefs about angels having wings
Beliefs about the creation of Adam
questions.answer: Beliefs that Allah has offspring, such as claims about a divine son, or that He was born from something/someone

questions.text: "وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ" means:
options: And there is none comparable/equal to Him
And He has many equals among creation
And His equal is found among the angels
And no one can worship Him properly
questions.answer: And there is none comparable/equal to Him

questions.text: How do these final two points connect back to "Ahad" (the One) at the surah's start?
options: They provide concrete proof of His uniqueness — no offspring, no origin, and no equal, all confirming He is truly One in every sense
They contradict the meaning of Ahad established earlier
They are unrelated statements added at random
They apply only to created beings, not to Allah
questions.answer: They provide concrete proof of His uniqueness — no offspring, no origin, and no equal, all confirming He is truly One in every sense

questions.text: What is the overall summary teaching of Surah Al-Ikhlas?
options: A complete, concise declaration of pure monotheism, refuting every form of shirk in Allah's Essence, attributes, and standing
A description of the Day of Judgment
A set of legal rulings for trade
A historical account of past nations
questions.answer: A complete, concise declaration of pure monotheism, refuting every form of shirk in Allah's Essence, attributes, and standing

stages.title: Al-Falaq (I) — Lord of the Daybreak
stages.description: Seeking refuge with the One who splits darkness into light

questions.text: "قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ" — what does "Al-Falaq" mean?
options: The daybreak/dawn (the splitting of darkness by light)
A mountain in Makkah
A specific type of tree
A river in Paradise
questions.answer: The daybreak/dawn (the splitting of darkness by light)

questions.text: Why is Allah specifically described as "Lord of the Daybreak" when seeking refuge in this surah?
options: Because just as He splits the darkness of night with light every day, He is capable of removing the darkness/harm of any evil sought refuge from
Because daybreak has no particular connection to seeking refuge
Because the surah is only about astronomy
Because daybreak is when evil is strongest
questions.answer: Because just as He splits the darkness of night with light every day, He is capable of removing the darkness/harm of any evil sought refuge from

questions.text: What kind of surah is Al-Falaq classified as, along with An-Nas?
options: A Surah of seeking refuge/protection (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn)
A Surah of legal rulings
A Surah of stories about past nations
A Surah about the Hajj
questions.answer: A Surah of seeking refuge/protection (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn)

questions.text: الفلق - ماذا يعني هذا الاسم؟
options: الصبح أو انشقاق الظلام عن النور
الليل الحالك الظلام
اسم جبل في مكة
اسم نهر في الجنة
questions.answer: الصبح أو انشقاق الظلام عن النور

questions.text: What is the general purpose of Surah Al-Falaq?
options: To teach the believer to seek Allah's protection from specific categories of evil
To describe the creation of the heavens
To narrate the story of a past prophet
To establish rulings on fasting
questions.answer: To teach the believer to seek Allah's protection from specific categories of evil

stages.title: Al-Falaq (II) — Evil of What He Created
stages.description: The broadest category of protection sought in this surah

questions.text: "مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ" means seeking refuge from:
options: The evil of whatever He (Allah) has created
The evil of Allah Himself
The evil of one specific animal only
The evil found only in the sea
questions.answer: The evil of whatever He (Allah) has created

questions.text: Why is this phrase considered comprehensive, covering the broadest category of evil in the surah?
options: Because it includes any harmful creation whatsoever — humans, animals, jinn, or anything else that could bring harm
Because it refers only to a single specific enemy
Because it excludes human beings from any possibility of harm
Because it applies only to natural disasters
questions.answer: Because it includes any harmful creation whatsoever — humans, animals, jinn, or anything else that could bring harm

questions.text: من شر ما خلق - هل هذا يشمل كل المخلوقات المؤذية؟
options: نعم، فهو عام يشمل كل شر يصدر من المخلوقات
لا، يقتصر على الحيوانات المفترسة فقط
لا، يقتصر على الجن فقط
لا، يقتصر على الإنس فقط
questions.answer: نعم، فهو عام يشمل كل شر يصدر من المخلوقات

questions.text: Why does the surah start with this general phrase before mentioning specific evils in later ayat?
options: To first establish broad protection, then highlight specific dangerous categories worth special mention
Because the specific evils mentioned later are unrelated to creation entirely
Because the general phrase is actually a mistake in ordering
Because the specific evils are less dangerous than the general one
questions.answer: To first establish broad protection, then highlight specific dangerous categories worth special mention

questions.text: What does seeking refuge from "the evil of what He created" teach about Allah's control over creation?
options: That Allah alone has full control and power over all of His creation, both good and harmful
That Allah has no control over harmful creatures
That creation acts independently of Allah's will
That evil exists outside of Allah's knowledge
questions.answer: That Allah alone has full control and power over all of His creation, both good and harmful

stages.title: Al-Falaq (III) — Evil of Darkness
stages.description: Seeking refuge from the night when it settles

questions.text: "وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ" refers to the evil of:
options: The night/darkness when it settles/spreads
The bright light of midday
The heat of summer
The sound of thunder
questions.answer: The night/darkness when it settles/spreads

questions.text: Why is nightfall specifically singled out as a time associated with potential evil?
options: Because harmful creatures, thieves, and evil actions are traditionally more active or hidden under the cover of darkness
Because nighttime has no spiritual significance at all
Because it is the safest time of day
Because the Qur'an never mentions daytime dangers
questions.answer: Because harmful creatures, thieves, and evil actions are traditionally more active or hidden under the cover of darkness

questions.text: غاسق إذا وقب - ماذا يعني هذا الوصف؟
options: الليل إذا اشتد ظلامه وانتشر
الصبح إذا أشرق
الشمس إذا ارتفعت
الرياح إذا هبت
questions.answer: الليل إذا اشتد ظلامه وانتشر

questions.text: How does this ayah's mention of darkness connect back to the surah's opening description of Allah as 'Lord of the Daybreak'?
options: It contrasts the darkness/evil being sought refuge from with the light/relief that Allah, as Lord of Daybreak, can bring
It has no connection to the opening at all
It shows that Allah has no power over darkness
It shows darkness is more powerful than daybreak in this surah
questions.answer: It contrasts the darkness/evil being sought refuge from with the light/relief that Allah, as Lord of Daybreak, can bring

questions.text: What lesson can be drawn about being cautious and remembering Allah especially at night?
options: Nighttime deserves extra mindfulness and remembrance of Allah due to its association with potential harm
Nighttime requires no special caution or remembrance at all
Remembrance of Allah is unnecessary once the sun sets
Night is only relevant to farmers, with no spiritual lesson
questions.answer: Nighttime deserves extra mindfulness and remembrance of Allah due to its association with potential harm

stages.title: Al-Falaq (IV) — Knot-Blowers & The Envier
stages.description: The final two evils named specifically in the surah

questions.text: "وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ" refers to the evil of:
options: Those who blow on knots (practicing magic/sorcery)
Those who tie ropes for building
Those who sew clothing
Those who fish using nets
questions.answer: Those who blow on knots (practicing magic/sorcery)

questions.text: "وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ" refers to the evil of:
options: An envier when he envies
A generous person when he gives
A traveler when he journeys
A teacher when he instructs
questions.answer: An envier when he envies

questions.text: Why is "when he envies" — specifically the act, not just the feeling — mentioned?
options: Because envy itself is a natural human feeling, but acting upon it to harm another is what's dangerous
Because feeling envy is impossible for human beings
Because acting on envy is always harmless
Because the phrase refers only to feeling envious, not acting on it
questions.answer: Because envy itself is a natural human feeling, but acting upon it to harm another is what's dangerous

questions.text: النفاثات في العقد - إلى ماذا تشير؟
options: إلى ممارسة السحر بالنفث في العقد
إلى صناعة الحبال العادية
إلى تعليم الخياطة
إلى بناء البيوت
questions.answer: إلى ممارسة السحر بالنفث في العقد

questions.text: What is the overall structure of the four categories of evil listed in Surah Al-Falaq?
options: General evil of creation, evil of darkness, evil of magic/sorcery, and evil of envy — moving from broad to specific dangers
All four categories describe the exact same evil repeated four times
The four categories are unrelated to each other with no logical order
They describe four different prophets
questions.answer: General evil of creation, evil of darkness, evil of magic/sorcery, and evil of envy — moving from broad to specific dangers

stages.title: An-Nas (I) — Three Attributes Invoked
stages.description: Rabb, Malik, and Ilah of mankind

questions.text: "قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ" — the first attribute of Allah invoked is:
options: Rabb (Lord) of mankind
Malik (King) of mankind
Ilah (God) of mankind
Rahman (Merciful) of mankind
questions.answer: Rabb (Lord) of mankind

questions.text: "مَلِكِ النَّاسِ" — the second attribute invoked is:
options: Malik (King/Sovereign) of mankind
Rabb (Lord) of mankind
Ilah (God) of mankind
Khaliq (Creator) of mankind
questions.answer: Malik (King/Sovereign) of mankind

questions.text: "إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ" — the third attribute invoked is:
options: Ilah (God/the One deserving worship) of mankind
Rabb (Lord) of mankind
Malik (King) of mankind
Samad (Self-Sufficient) of mankind
questions.answer: Ilah (God/the One deserving worship) of mankind

questions.text: Why does the surah build up through Rabb, then Malik, then Ilah in that specific order?
options: It moves from Lordship (creation & sustenance), to Sovereignty (authority & rule), to Divinity (the right to be worshipped) — an increasingly powerful basis for seeking refuge
The order has no particular significance and is random
It moves from the least powerful attribute to a lesser one
It repeats the same meaning three times with no progression
questions.answer: It moves from Lordship (creation & sustenance), to Sovereignty (authority & rule), to Divinity (the right to be worshipped) — an increasingly powerful basis for seeking refuge

questions.text: رب الناس، ملك الناس، إله الناس - ما الحكمة من ذكر هذه الصفات الثلاث؟
options: لبيان أن من يستعاذ به يجب أن يكون ربا ومالكا ومعبودا بحق
لأنها أسماء لثلاثة آلهة مختلفة
لأنها صفات خاصة بالملائكة فقط
لا حكمة معروفة لذكرها
questions.answer: لبيان أن من يستعاذ به يجب أن يكون ربا ومالكا ومعبودا بحق

stages.title: An-Nas (II) — The Retreating Whisperer
stages.description: Al-Waswas Al-Khannas — the one who hides at remembrance of Allah

questions.text: "مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ" refers to the evil of:
options: The whisperer who withdraws/retreats (commonly understood as Shaytan)
A loud, open enemy
A wild animal
A natural disaster
questions.answer: The whisperer who withdraws/retreats (commonly understood as Shaytan)

questions.text: What does "Al-Khannas" specifically describe about this whisperer?
options: That he retreats and hides whenever Allah is remembered, but returns to whisper again when one is heedless
That he never leaves a person alone under any circumstance
That he only appears once in a person's lifetime
That he is visible to the human eye
questions.answer: That he retreats and hides whenever Allah is remembered, but returns to whisper again when one is heedless

questions.text: الوسواس الخناس - لماذا سمي بـ"الخناس"؟
options: لأنه يختفي وينسحب عند ذكر الله ويعود عند الغفلة
لأنه يظهر فقط في الليل
لأنه كائن مرئي بالعين
لأنه يهرب من النور فقط
questions.answer: لأنه يختفي وينسحب عند ذكر الله ويعود عند الغفلة

questions.text: What practical lesson does understanding 'Al-Khannas' give a believer?
options: That regularly remembering Allah (dhikr) is one's main defense, since the whisperer retreats specifically at that remembrance
That there is no practical defense against this whisperer
That physical strength alone can defeat this whisperer
That avoiding people entirely is the only defense
questions.answer: That regularly remembering Allah (dhikr) is one's main defense, since the whisperer retreats specifically at that remembrance

questions.text: Is this whisperer limited only to an unseen entity (Shaytan), according to the surah's continuation?
options: No — the following ayah clarifies the whispering comes from among both jinn and mankind
Yes, it refers exclusively to Shaytan with no other source
Yes, it refers exclusively to angels
The surah does not clarify this at all
questions.answer: No — the following ayah clarifies the whispering comes from among both jinn and mankind

stages.title: An-Nas (III) — From Jinn and Men
stages.description: The whispering that can come from either source

questions.text: "الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ" means this whisperer:
options: Whispers into the chests/hearts of people
Speaks openly and loudly to people
Only whispers to animals
Whispers only during sleep
questions.answer: Whispers into the chests/hearts of people

questions.text: "مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ" clarifies that this whispering can come from:
options: Both jinn and human beings
Angels only
Animals only
The Prophet ﷺ himself
questions.answer: Both jinn and human beings

questions.text: How can a human being act as a 'whisperer' in the same sense as Shaytan?
options: By tempting, misguiding, or planting evil suggestions in others' hearts, similar to how Shaytan whispers evil
Humans cannot ever act this way; only Shaytan can
By simply speaking any words at all to another person
By performing acts of worship in public
questions.answer: By tempting, misguiding, or planting evil suggestions in others' hearts, similar to how Shaytan whispers evil

questions.text: من الجنة والناس - ما الدرس المستفاد من ذكر الإنس هنا؟
options: أن بعض البشر قد يكونون سببا في الوسوسة والإغواء كما يفعل الشيطان
أن الإنس لا يمكن أن يوسوسوا إطلاقا
أن هذا يخص الجن فقط دون الإنس
لا علاقة لذكر الإنس بموضوع السورة
questions.answer: أن بعض البشر قد يكونون سببا في الوسوسة والإغواء كما يفعل الشيطان

questions.text: Why is it fitting that the very last ayah of the Qur'an ends by broadening the source of evil to include mankind as well as jinn?
options: It gives a complete, comprehensive warning covering every possible source of whispered evil a person may face
It suggests that jinn are no longer a real threat
It contradicts everything mentioned earlier in the surah
It has no particular significance for the Qur'an's closing
questions.answer: It gives a complete, comprehensive warning covering every possible source of whispered evil a person may face

stages.title: An-Nas (IV) — Closing Review: Al-Mu'awwidhatayn
stages.description: How Al-Falaq and An-Nas function together, closing the circle of this course

questions.text: What do Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas have in common in their function?
options: Both are surahs specifically for seeking Allah's protection (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn), recommended for daily protection
Both are legal rulings on marriage
Both describe the story of Prophet Musa
Both were revealed in Madinah after the Hijrah only
questions.answer: Both are surahs specifically for seeking Allah's protection (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn), recommended for daily protection

questions.text: What did the Prophet ﷺ recommend reciting these two surahs (along with Al-Ikhlas) for, according to hadith?
options: Protection, often recited three times morning and evening, and before sleeping while blowing into the hands and wiping the body
Only for reciting during the Hajj
Only for funerals
Only once in a lifetime
questions.answer: Protection, often recited three times morning and evening, and before sleeping while blowing into the hands and wiping the body

questions.text: How does the whole journey of this course — from Al-Isti'adhah to An-Nas — form a complete circle?
options: It begins by teaching how to seek refuge in Allah before reciting the Qur'an, and ends with the most detailed surahs specifically about seeking refuge from evil
It has no thematic connection from beginning to end
It begins and ends with the same exact surah
The beginning and end are about completely unrelated topics with no design
questions.answer: It begins by teaching how to seek refuge in Allah before reciting the Qur'an, and ends with the most detailed surahs specifically about seeking refuge from evil

questions.text: What is the shared root meaning between "أَعُوذُ" in Al-Isti'adhah and the refrain in Al-Falaq/An-Nas?
options: The concept of seeking protection/refuge (from the root ع-و-ذ)
The concept of praising Allah
The concept of seeking forgiveness
The concept of giving charity
questions.answer: The concept of seeking protection/refuge (from the root ع-و-ذ)

questions.text: What is one major lesson that ties together the short Surahs of Juz Amma studied in this course?
options: That true success comes from sincere Tawhid, righteous character, and constant reliance on and protection from Allah in every affair of life
That wealth is the ultimate measure of success in this life
That only ritual worship matters, with no connection to character
That these surahs have no unifying theme at all
questions.answer: That true success comes from sincere Tawhid, righteous character, and constant reliance on and protection from Allah in every affair of life

stages.title: Murāja'ah — Capstone Review
stages.description: A final review across every surah studied in this course

questions.text: Which surah's central theme is the four conditions for salvation: faith, righteous deeds, advising to truth, and advising to patience?
options: Surah Al-'Asr
Surah Al-Kawthar
Surah Al-Fil
Surah An-Nasr
questions.answer: Surah Al-'Asr

questions.text: Which surah describes the fate of Abraha's army as being made 'like eaten straw'?
options: Surah Al-Fil
Surah Quraysh
Surah Al-Masad
Surah Al-Kafirun
questions.answer: Surah Al-Fil

questions.text: Which surah connects gratitude for Allah's blessings with the commands to pray and offer sacrifice?
options: Surah Al-Kawthar
Surah Al-Ikhlas
Surah Al-Humazah
Surah Al-Falaq
questions.answer: Surah Al-Kawthar

questions.text: Which surah firmly declares no compromise in worship between the believer and disbeliever, ending with 'Lakum deenukum wa liya deen'?
options: Surah Al-Kafirun
Surah Al-Ma'un
Surah An-Nas
Surah Al-Masad
questions.answer: Surah Al-Kafirun

questions.text: Which surah is considered equal to one-third of the Qur'an due to its pure declaration of Tawhid?
options: Surah Al-Ikhlas
Surah Al-Fatihah
Surah An-Nasr
Surah Quraysh
questions.answer: Surah Al-Ikhlas

questions.text: Which two surahs together are known as Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (the two surahs of seeking refuge)?
options: Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas
Surah Al-Fatihah and Surah Al-Ikhlas
Surah Al-Kawthar and Surah Al-Kafirun
Surah Al-'Asr and Surah Al-Humazah
questions.answer: Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas

questions.text: Which surah was revealed as a direct warning to a named individual, the Prophet's ﷺ own uncle?
options: Surah Al-Masad
Surah An-Nasr
Surah Al-Fil
Surah Al-Ma'un
questions.answer: Surah Al-Masad

questions.text: Which behavior do Surah Al-Humazah and Surah Al-Ma'un both, in different ways, warn against?
options: Harming others through cruelty, mockery, or neglecting compassion
Traveling for trade
Reciting the Qur'an aloud
Building places of worship
questions.answer: Harming others through cruelty, mockery, or neglecting compassion
